In the rest frame of the glass the light travels with the usual reduced speed

u′ = c/n = 1/n  (since we set c = 1).

The glass itself moves in the laboratory frame with speed v in the same direction as the light.  
To obtain the light speed u in the lab frame we use the relativistic velocity–addition formula (for collinear velocities):

u = (u′ + v) / (1 + u′ v).

Insert u′ = 1/n:

u = (1/n + v) / (1 + v/n).

Multiply numerator and denominator by n:

u = (1 + n v) / (n + v).

Hence the speed of light in the glass relative to the laboratory is

u = (1 + n v)/(n + v),

which corresponds to option (D).

Answer: D
